title: Arbitration and conciliation outside court — general guidance
content: Parties with arbitration clauses or mutual consent may use private arbitration or conciliation instead of litigation. Awards may be recognised and enforced through the courts. Keep the arbitration agreement and award documents.

title: Chiefs and elders community resolution — general guidance
citation: National Government Coordination Act; ADR guidance
content: Chiefs and village elders help resolve local disputes over boundaries, family matters and minor claims through dialogue. Unresolved or serious matters are referred to courts or relevant offices. Keep any written settlement or referral letter issued.

title: Documents to keep for any case — general guidance
content: For any legal issue keep identification, contracts, receipts, messages, photos, OB or reference numbers, and a dated timeline of events. Organise originals and copies separately. These are routinely required by police, lawyers, tribunals, and courts.

title: Affidavits for lost documents
content: Swear loss affidavits with document details, OB numbers where applicable, and commissioner stamps for replacements. Keep commissioned copies.

title: Late birth registration
content: Late registration needs clinic cards, affidavits, and chief letters with fees. Start early for school and IDs. Keep notification slips.

title: Certifying documents
content: Certify copies with commissioners or issuing offices for filings. Keep certification receipts with the bundle.

title: When offices ask for chief letters
content: Chiefs confirm residence, family, and events with IDs and witnesses. Attend with documents and neighbours where needed. Keep stamped copies.

title: Reporting dead livestock or disease
content: Report sudden deaths to veterinary officers without moving carcasses. Keep treatment and vaccination records.

title: Disability registration and card
content: Assess at county hospitals, then register with the National Council for services and tax considerations. Keep assessment reports and the card.

title: Building a case file that wins
content: Keep IDs, contracts, receipts, messages, photos, and reference numbers in one dated file with originals separate. Organised files get faster help at every office. Update the timeline after each event.

title: Setting up eCitizen correctly
content: Register with your ID, verified phone, and email with strong passwords. Link KRA, NTSA, and BRS services. Keep login recovery details safe.

title: FIDA-Kenya for women and children
content: FIDA supports women and children on family, GBV, and succession matters through clinics and representation. Carry IDs and case documents. Keep intake references.

title: Filing nil and normal returns
content: File income returns yearly even where income is nil to avoid penalties, with P9 and business records. Keep filing receipts.

title: Help after fires
content: Report to fire services, police, and chiefs with loss lists for relief and investigations. Keep OB, photos, and assistance records.

title: First aid after injuries
content: Stop bleeding, call emergency services, and preserve the scene for investigators. Keep treatment records for claims.

title: Help after floods and disasters
content: Report to chiefs and Red Cross with damage photos for relief and assessment. Keep loss lists and assistance records.

title: Reporting illegal dumping
content: Report dumping with photos and locations to county environment and NEMA. Use licensed collectors. Keep receipts and references.

title: Police clearance for jobs
content: Apply on eCitizen with fingerprints at gazetted centres for job and travel clearance. Keep the payment receipt and certificate.

title: University funding model appeals
content: Appeal banding with household and admission evidence within timelines. Meet documentation checklists. Keep award and appeal records.

title: Kituo cha Sheria legal aid
content: Kituo offers legal aid on evictions, employment, and criminal matters through offices and clinics. Book with documents ready. Keep appointment records.

title: New electricity connections
content: Apply with IDs, plot, and wiring certificates, paying official fees. Avoid middlemen. Keep application and payment records.

title: Getting a KRA PIN
content: Apply on iTax with ID and details, then collect the PIN certificate. Update details on changes. Keep the certificate secure.

title: Paying land rates and rent
content: Pay county rates and national ground rent before penalties block transfers. Keep demand notes and clearance receipts.

title: Getting counselling help
content: Reach counsellors, helplines, and clinics early; emergencies go to hospitals. Helplines include 1199 and 0800 720 640 referrals. Keep referral records.

title: Preserving chats and messages
content: Export full chats with dates, back up media, and avoid edits. Screenshots supplement but exports prove context. Keep originals and exports.

title: Separate meters in rentals
content: Agree meter separation costs and billing in writing with the landlord before splitting. Keep agreements and installer receipts.

title: Getting help from NLAS
content: Apply at NLAS centres with IDs, case documents, and income proof; the toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Follow up with the file reference. Keep the reference and appointment slips.

title: Reporting noise pollution
content: Log dates and times with recordings, then report to NEMA, county, or police. Night violations attract enforcement. Keep the diary and references.

title: NSSF self-registration
content: Self-employed persons register with ID and contribute monthly for benefits. Keep the member number and payment records.

title: Cash transfers for older persons
content: Enroll through social development officers with IDs for Inua Jamii consideration. Report payment failures with records. Keep enrollment slips.

title: Originals vs copies
content: Courts prefer originals; keep them safe and file certified copies where required. Never alter originals. Keep a copy log.

title: Support for orphans and vulnerable children
content: Report to children officers for placement, schooling, and cash-transfer consideration with birth and death records. Keep officer contacts and records.

title: Applying for a passport
content: Apply on eCitizen with birth certificate, IDs, photos, and recommender details. Book biometrics. Keep application references.

title: Storing fuel at home safely
content: Avoid storing petrol indoors; use approved containers away from flames. Report illegal dens. Keep purchase receipts from licensed stations.

title: Photos that count as evidence
content: Take wide, medium, and close shots with dates, locations, and intact metadata. Back up originals. Keep printed and digital sets.

title: Getting a police abstract
content: Apply at the reporting station with the OB number and IDs, pay the fee, and collect the signed abstract. Keep the abstract for insurers and registries.

title: Prepaid water meters
content: Top up through official channels with meter numbers and keep tokens. Dispute faulty deductions with readings. Keep token records.

title: Pro bono and university law clinics
citation: Legal aid and clinical education guidance
content: Law school clinics and LSK pro bono schemes assist qualifying matters with documents and merit screening. Apply with the full file. Keep referral letters.

title: Bursaries and CDF applications
content: Apply with fee structures, results, and chief letters before deadlines at ward offices. Keep application receipts and award letters.

title: Registering for SHIF (SHA)
content: Register households with IDs and dependants through SHA channels and confirm facility empanelment. Keep registration and contribution records.

title: Tax compliance certificates
content: Clear returns and debts before applying for TCC needed for tenders and jobs. Keep the certificate and renewal dates.

title: Writing a clear incident timeline
content: List dates, places, people, and what happened in order with supporting documents per entry. Timelines expose gaps and deadlines. Keep the timeline updated.

title: Translating documents for filings
content: Translate foreign-language documents with certified translators for court and registry use. Keep translator certificates.

title: Tree planting and chief permits
content: Source seedlings from licensed nurseries and confirm planting sites with chiefs where public land is used. Keep seedling receipts.

title: New water connections
content: Apply to the county provider with IDs and plot details, pay connection fees officially. Keep application and payment records.

title: Recording witness details early
content: Note names, contacts, and what each witness saw with dates. Memories fade fast. Keep the list with the timeline.

title: Basic education rights and school fees — general guidance
content: Every child in Kenya has a right to free and compulsory basic education, and public schools should not impose unlawful levies beyond approved charges. Parents facing exclusion over fees or uniforms can escalate to head teachers, boards, and county education officers. Keep fee structures, receipts, and admission records.

title: Citizenship, IDs and passports — general guidance
content: Kenyan citizenship by birth, registration, or naturalisation supports access to IDs, passports, and other civil documents through immigration and civil registration offices. Applicants should use official eCitizen channels and carry original supporting documents. Keep application references, receipts, and birth records.

title: Rights of persons with disabilities — general guidance
content: Persons with disabilities in Kenya are entitled to dignity, access, reasonable accommodation, and protection from discrimination in work, school, and services. Registration with the National Council for Persons with Disabilities supports access to programmes and tax considerations. Keep assessment reports, registration cards, and correspondence.

title: Medical negligence complaints — general guidance
citation: Health Act, 2017; Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council Act
content: Patients who suffer harm from suspected negligent care in Kenya can complain to the facility, the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council, or other professional boards. Clear treatment records and timelines are important for review and redress. Keep discharge summaries, receipts, prescriptions, and test results.

title: HELB loans and student funding appeals — general guidance
content: Students in Kenyan universities and colleges can apply for HELB loans and scholarships under the prevailing funding model and appeal where allocations seem incorrect. Applicants should meet deadlines and provide accurate household and admission details. Keep application records, award letters, and disbursement statements.

title: NEMA approvals and environmental impact assessment — general guidance
content: Projects likely to affect the environment in Kenya, such as factories, quarries, and large developments, generally require NEMA approval and sometimes a full environmental impact assessment. Affected neighbours can participate during public consultation and raise objections. Keep project notices, submissions, and NEMA correspondence.

title: Noise pollution complaints — general guidance
content: Excessive noise from bars, churches, construction, or events can be reported to NEMA, county environment officers, or police, especially at night. Complainants should record dates, times, and the source to support enforcement. Keep a noise diary and any reports or reference numbers.

title: Protection and support for older persons — general guidance
content: Older persons in Kenya facing neglect, abuse, or property exploitation can seek help from chiefs, social development officers, and police alongside available cash transfer programmes. Families should arrange care, medical support, and safe handling of pensions and property. Keep medical records, payment records, and report references.

title: SHIF registration and health coverage — general guidance
content: The Social Health Insurance Fund has replaced NHIF as Kenya's public health cover, with registration and means-tested contributions for households. Members should confirm registration, dependants, and facility empanelment before seeking care. Keep registration details, contribution receipts, and hospital invoices.

title: Solid waste and dumping complaints — general guidance
citation: Environmental Management and Co-ordination Act, 1999; County by-laws
content: Illegal dumping, burning of waste, and discharge of effluent can be reported to county public health officers and NEMA for enforcement. Households and businesses should use licensed collectors and keep premises clean. Keep photos, collection receipts, and complaint reference numbers.

title: Water use rights and permits — general guidance
content: Abstraction of water from rivers, lakes, or boreholes in Kenya generally requires authorisation from the Water Resources Authority alongside any county service connection. Illegal connections, pollution of water sources, and interference with meters can attract penalties. Keep permits, bills, and payment receipts.

title: Work permits and refugee protection — general guidance
citation: Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Act, 2011; Refugees Act, 2021
content: Foreign nationals working in Kenya generally need the correct class of work permit, while asylum seekers and refugees register with the Department of Refugee Services for protection documents. Employers and landlords should verify valid permits rather than retain originals. Keep permit copies, receipts, and appointment slips.

title: Legal aid eligibility in Kenya — general guidance
content: State legal aid prioritises indigent persons, children, persons with disabilities and others facing serious injustice without means to pay. Eligibility is assessed through means and merit tests. Keep income documents and case papers for the assessment interview.

title: Hakili is not a lawyer — general guidance
content: Hakili prepares checklists and organises information from verified passages and user documents. It does not give legal advice or predict outcomes. Confirm every plan with a qualified lawyer, paralegal, or the National Legal Aid Service before acting.

title: Deadlines must be verified — general guidance
content: Time limits for notices, appeals, complaints, and filings vary widely and change over time. Never rely on memory or hearsay for a deadline. Confirm the current limit with the relevant office, the statute, or a legal aid provider and diarise it.
